user_prompt: What is the effect of mobile phone reminders (SMS text messages and/or phone calls, including automated voice calls) sent to parents or caregivers, compared with routine immunisation care without reminders, on receipt of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3 / DPT3 / pentavalent-3 / Penta-3) in children in low- and middle-income countries?  Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) using a random-effects model. RR > 1 means more children received DTP3/Penta-3 in the reminder arm (favours reminders).  Outcome: number of children who received DTP3/Penta-3 (events) out of the number randomised to each arm (total), at the study's main follow-up assessment for that dose (e.g. by 14 weeks, 18 weeks, 6 months or 12 months of age). - Extract raw event counts for each arm. If only percentages are reported, convert them to counts using the number randomised in that arm. - Use crude (unadjusted) counts. Do not use adjusted odds ratios, logistic-regression estimates or cluster-adjusted (GEE) risk ratios when raw counts are available, and do not convert an odds ratio into the result. - Use intention-to-treat denominators (all randomised/enrolled participants per arm), not per-protocol or "children seen at follow-up" subsets, when both are reported. - Use the outcome "received / completed Penta-3 (DTP3)" at the primary follow-up. Do not use "timely receipt within 1 week of the due date" or "received without delay" if overall receipt is also reported. - If a study reports the three pentavalent doses separately, use only the third dose (or "completed all 3 doses"). - Multi-arm trials: use the arm receiving reminders only (SMS/phone call alone) as the treatment group and the no-reminder routine-care arm as the control. Ignore arms that combine reminders with monetary or other incentives, education-only arms and other co-interventions.  Do not pool measles, BCG, OPV, yellow fever, "fully immunised" or "all scheduled vaccines" outcomes, timeliness or delay outcomes, or costs. Include only randomised controlled trials (individual or cluster); exclude non-randomised and controlled before-after studies.
